idea: A KD tree divides Cartesian space along alternating axes. A subtree can be skipped when its split plane is farther away than the current search bound.
steps: Median-split points recursively by X then Y.
Search the nearer branch and maintain the best k points in a max-heap.
Visit the far branch only when its split plane could improve the result.
example: Four points one unit from the origin tie on distance; names break ties deterministically.
concepts: Comparisons avoid square roots until display.
A lower bound rejects regions that cannot improve the answer.
Equal coordinates and large k can force a nearly full scan.
question: Does a KD tree guarantee logarithmic queries?
answer: No. Its performance depends on dimension and geometry; worst-case search still visits every point.
challenge: Use Equal distances, then set the radius to exactly one.
cost: Build O(n log² n) with repeated sorting; average queries often prune well, worst case O(n log k).
